eye: peripheral vision, one eye, stimulus 30 degrees off straight-ahead gaze
method: behavioural: visual-grasp gaze shift to a checkerboard dropped into a uniform orange background, threshold at half-maximal response
conditions: adult males; stimulus 21.0 cm from the eye; diffuse light about 30.7 and 0.41 umol m-2 s-1 (results give 1.22 and 1.18 cycles/degree for the two)

source.authors: Fleishman LJ, Yeo AI, Perez CW
source.title: Visual acuity and signal color pattern in an Anolis lizard

where: Abstract; Methods and Results read through WebFetch of the publisher page (summarised, sentence asked for verbatim)
quote: The acuity threshold was 1.21 cycles deg−1.
note: Peripheral acuity of A. sagrei only (10 and 8 males in two experiments). The foveal figures in the paper are calculated from published A. carolinensis anatomy, not measured here, and are not logged. Authors caveat: low-light responsiveness fell over time; stimuli mixed colour and luminance contrast, so luminance probably set the threshold.
